summary: Audit A4 (validation outside California) in docs/redesign/audit-3/validation.md, revised after an independent review. Fires outside California cannot be built today: the CLI, catalog and pipeline know CAL FIRE incidents only (the year is not the blocker). Four more blockers would make the scores wrong: perimeters filtered to US-CA; UTM zone only 10 or 11 (Table Rock SC: scale 1.127, 21.4 degree rotation; the standard zone formula leaves California unchanged); fires of federal FY2024 get LF2024 fuels that already hold their own burn (Horse Gulch, Windy Deuce need LF2023; Rush, a FY2025 fire, correctly gets LF2024), and a failed fetch can fall forward to a newer edition; and the California live-fuel-moisture table makes February Texas grass and March Appalachian fuels green. New in the revision: Open-Meteo's daily 10,000-call cap on the shared cloud IP is the main schedule risk for validation (R7 now P0: stop, do not fill with ERA5); Madre is missing, so stage D starts by rebuilding it and re-measuring the California baseline; LF2025 is NoData in the South and East until November 2026. Test set: the 12 fires of user decision round 2 (two per region), with ids, IrwinIDs, points, expected fuels edition and UTM zone, and pre-registered UTC starts; Windy Deuce's starts move to its first perimeter (65 % of its area burned in the first 6 h). Accuracy label: GACC regions (Southern Area split TX/OK vs the rest), the mean of per-fire mean growth Sorensen (OSCC 0.43), a score only with at least 2 fires and 16 leads; Public shows words with the score one tap away, Command the score; in-sample, fuel and start caveats; JSON data file shape with per-region method fields.

notes_for_integrator: P0 R1 (backend pipeline role): build a past national fire by IRWIN id. Use the id {UTC year}-{slug(IncidentName)}-{IrwinID hex[:6]} with the SPEC 4.4 regex. Change catalog.get_summary (catalog.py:317-354), cli.resolve_incident (cli.py:75-109), pipeline.build_incident (pipeline.py:466-469) and is_catalog_incident/spec_incident_id (pipeline.py:71-91). The year is not the blocker: catalog.py:332-342 already resolves CAL FIRE ids of other years; the blocker is the CAL FIRE-only record source.

P0 R2: sources/perimeters.py:80 STATE='US-CA' (used at :181,:326,:538). Query by attr_IrwinID='{...}' OR poly_IRWINID when the IRWIN id is known; otherwise use the fire's own POOState. Keep the oversize check.

P0 R3: grid.py:59-61 utm_epsg_for. Use the zone floor((lon+180)/6)+1 and EPSG 32600+zone; update SPEC 4.1 (SPEC.md:119-120). The web reads manifest.grid.utm_zone generically, but its tests cover only zones 10 and 11.

P0 R4: sources/landfire.py:34 EDITIONS add 'LF2023'. edition_for(mode, started_ms): historical = LF{federal FY of ignition - 1} (FY starts Oct 1: Jul 2024 -> LF2023, Oct 2024 (Rush) -> LF2024, Aug 2025 -> LF2024, Oct 2025+ -> LF2025), live = LF2025. Change the caller build/aoi.py:356 (pass ctx.summary.started_ms) and the fallback at aoi.py:285, which today tries LF2025 for any other edition: a historical build must fall back only to an older edition, with a warning, also where the edition is NoData (LF2025 outside SW/NW until Nov 2026; audit A1 R8). Refuse fires before Oct 2023 unless forced. Update pipeline.py:568, tests test_terrain.py:213-283,438, test_pipeline.py:42, test_pipeline_support.py:145, and SPEC.md:63,494. California behaviour change: historical FY2026 CA fires move to LF2025; Eaton, Palisades, Madre stay LF2024.
